metadata.goal: Analyze variability in repeated urban trips across multiple users.
metadata.category: Repeated trips for multiple Montréal users with repeat context, day type, purpose, mode, route deviation, route directness, timing, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 20 Multi User Repeated Trip Variability
metadata.dataset_description: Repeated trips for multiple Montréal users with repeat context, day type, purpose, mode, route deviation, route directness, timing, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.metric_note: Distances are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; average point speed and duration are synchronized with the point table. Montréal's long island axis runs approximately southwest–northeast, so signed axis displacement summarizes the dominant travel direction.

plot.title: Repeated-trip Timing, Mode, and Directness
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do weekday-morning work repeats differ from work repeats at other times?
insight_list.insight: Work trips between similar locations are more mode-consistent, temporally concentrated, and route-direct on weekday mornings than at other times.

plot.title: User Route and Speed Variability
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Among similarly long repeated trips, which users follow stable routes and which show greater route and speed variation?
insight_list.insight: For similarly long trips, some users repeatedly travel between the same locations along similar routes, while others take varied routes with larger speed fluctuations.

plot.title: Weekend Purpose, Time, Mode, and Route Shifts
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do weekend repeats differ from weekday work repeats?
insight_list.insight: Weekend repeats more often shift to shopping or leisure, depart later, and use different modes or routes than weekday repeats.

insights: Work trips between similar locations are more mode-consistent, temporally concentrated, and route-direct on weekday mornings than at other times.
For similarly long trips, some users repeatedly travel between the same locations along similar routes, while others take varied routes with larger speed fluctuations.
Weekend repeats more often shift to shopping or leisure, depart later, and use different modes or routes than weekday repeats.
summary: Weekday-morning work repeats are the most temporally concentrated, mode-consistent, and direct. Users separate into stable- and variable-route patterns, while weekend repeats shift toward later shopping or leisure travel with different modes and routes.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
